references.text: Describes the use of the shofar (trumpet) on festival days and holy occasions, including new moon days and days of joy, illustrating the broader use of the shofar in Israelite worship.
Refers to the first day of the seventh month as a day of trumpet blowing (teruah), connecting the holy days of the seventh month.
Describes the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) on the tenth day of the seventh month, which is the same day mentioned in Leviticus 25:9.
Refers to the festival on the first day of the seventh month with teruah (trumpet blast), which inaugurates the holy days before the Day of Atonement.
Provides further details about the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month, which is the context for the proclamation of the Jubilee year.
Mentions the shofar (ram's horn) in connection with the revelation at Sinai, showing the significance of the shofar in sacred contexts.
Describes the extremely powerful sound of the shofar at Sinai, demonstrating the instrument's role in divine revelations.
Relates the use of the shofar at the fall of Jericho, where priests blew horns as a sign of God's intervention.
Uses the image of the shofar to proclaim, connecting proclamation with freedom and restoration, as the Jubilee year does.
Speaks of proclaiming liberty for captives and a year of favor from the Lord, which is thematically linked to the proclamation of the Jubilee year.
Mentions the year of release (the Jubilee year) in the context of property rights, illustrating the practical application of the Jubilee year.
